motorglider.name: Motor glider
motorglider.notice: Motor gliders differ a lot in power, weight and behaviour. The sources describe powered model aeroplanes in general, so the instructions do not fit every motor glider.

view.badgeSide: You see the model from the side
view.hintPilot: View from your place, zoomed in
view.cuesHint: Speed cues are an illustration: they show relative speed, not measured values.

transmitter.title: Transmitter
transmitter.trail: Yellow trail = stick path of the last second

strip.title: The figure at a glance

reliability.title: How reliable is this?
reliability.p1: Every instruction here is confirmed by at least two independent sources: different authors, not copies of each other. Where sources disagree or say nothing, the app says so instead of filling the gap.
reliability.p2: The animation is an illustration. The timing is slow motion, and stick travel is drawn on one scale (little, half, strong, full). These are not measured values.
reliability.p3: Models differ. Set-up, power, wind and propeller direction change what is needed, so the values are guideline values. Check them in a simulator or with an experienced pilot.
reliability.legendConfirmed: Confirmed: at least two independent sources agree.
reliability.legendDisputed: Sources disagree: the sources contradict each other.
reliability.legendGap: No confirmed instruction: the sources say nothing, or only one source does.
reliability.legendIllustration: Illustration: shown in the animation, but not confirmed by the sources.

footer.colours: Top side teal with the canopy, underside coral. The control surfaces move as the sticks move. A control surface with deflection glows yellow-orange (stronger = more deflection) and fades for about a second, also in the control schematic (▲ = trailing edge up, ▼ = down). Yellow waves at the sticks are constant small corrections.

knife-edge.name: Knife edge
knife-edge.idea: The model flies straight on its side. The rudder holds it there.

instructions.across: Fly the pass across your front, left to right or right to left.
instructions.height: For the first attempts, start with plenty of height.

instructions.quarter-roll: Roll with the aileron from level flight until the wings are about vertical (a quarter turn).
instructions.rudder-opposite: From upright flight, add rudder opposite to the roll: roll right, rudder left; roll left, rudder right.
instructions.two-steps: While learning, practise the quarter roll first without rudder, and add the rudder once the <bank>bank</bank> is set.

instructions.rudder-holds: The rudder carries the model on its side. Without it, the model does not stay there.
instructions.rudder-cue: Cue: <canopy>canopy</canopy> toward you, rudder stick toward the tail; belly toward you, rudder stick toward the nose.
instructions.rudder-amount: How much rudder you need depends on the model and its speed. Faster flight needs less.
instructions.tuck: Rudder makes the nose tuck. Which way depends on the model: toward the <landingGear>landing gear</landingGear> or toward the canopy.
instructions.tuck-elevator: Correct the tuck with the elevator. If the nose tucks toward the landing gear, give a little up elevator.
instructions.roll-aileron: If the model starts to roll, correct with a little aileron. The direction depends on the model.
instructions.throttle-height: The throttle adds or removes height: if the model sinks, add throttle.

notes.altitude: Sources disagree on what holds the height: some say the rudder does, others say the rudder only sets the nose angle and the throttle holds the height.
notes.duration: How long to hold the <knifeEdge>knife edge</knifeEdge>: the sources give no confirmed value.

instructions.quarter-back: Roll a quarter turn back with the aileron to upright, and take the rudder and elevator inputs off.

illustration.sides: Which side of the model faces you, and the exact stick travel and timing, are an illustration. The sources give the rules above, not these values.

elevator.name: Elevator
elevator.idea: The model sinks on a steep to nearly vertical line with the elevator pulled fully, nose high and stalled.

instructions.slow-to-stall: Slow the model down to the stall: cut or reduce the throttle and pull up elevator.
instructions.progressive: Pull the elevator smoothly, not abruptly.
instructions.from-downline: You can also start from a short downline: pull full up elevator quickly to shed the speed.

instructions.full-up: Hold the elevator pulled fully, or almost fully.
instructions.steep-descent: The model sinks on a steep to nearly vertical line.
instructions.throttle-little: Add a little throttle to keep the nose up. Changing the throttle moves the nose up or down.
instructions.rudder-heading: The rudder corrects the heading, left and right.
instructions.aileron-small: Catch a rocking wing with small, brief aileron inputs.

notes.throttle: Throttle in the hold: most sources add a little throttle, one source says idle.
notes.levelling: What levels the wings: some sources say mainly the rudder, others say the ailerons.

instructions.release: To fly out, release the up elevator and add throttle.
instructions.into-harrier: You can also exit into a <harrier>harrier</harrier> instead of flying out.

notes.min-height: How low you may go before the exit: the sources give no confirmed value.

harrier.name: Harrier
harrier.idea: Slow flight with the nose about 45° up. The elevator sets the nose attitude, the throttle holds the height.

instructions.rates: Practise with high control rates switched on.

instructions.reduce-and-pull: Reduce the throttle while you feed in up elevator gradually.
instructions.from-elevator: Coming from an elevator: add throttle until the sinking stops and the model moves forward.

notes.throttle-entry: Throttle as the model slows in the entry: three sources reduce the throttle while adding up elevator, two add throttle together with the up elevator to hold height.

instructions.elevator-attitude: The elevator holds the nose attitude. The throttle decides whether the model holds its height.
instructions.more-thrust: The <harrier>harrier</harrier> needs clearly more thrust than ordinary slow flight.
instructions.throttle-pumps: Use the throttle actively in short pumps instead of setting it once.
instructions.rudder-rolls: Rudder also rolls the model the same way: rudder left rolls it left.
instructions.torque-rudder: With a standard <propeller>propeller</propeller> rotation, hold some right rudder against the propeller <torque>torque</torque>.

notes.aileron: <aileron>Aileron</aileron> in the harrier: one manufacturer manual says to avoid it because it may snap the model. Other sources use small aileron inputs to keep the wings level.
notes.angle-value: Nose angle: four sources say about 45 degrees, one says about 60 degrees or more, with the elevator held at maximum for most models.

instructions.throttle-up: Raise the throttle toward full and lower the nose with the elevator so the model regains speed.
instructions.emergency: If the figure goes wrong, go to full throttle.

hover.name: Hover
hover.idea: The model hangs vertically on its propeller. The throttle holds the height.

instructions.safe-height: Practise at a safe height and hold the <hover>hover</hover> only briefly at first.

notes.start-height: Starting height: the sources give very different values, so none is shown.

instructions.from-harrier: Enter from a <harrier>harrier</harrier>: keep adding up <elevator>elevator</elevator> until the model is vertical.

notes.entry-orientation: Which way you fly at entry and which side of the model faces you: the sources do not say.
notes.entry-start: Where the pull-up starts: two sources start from a harrier, one from level flight at moderate speed.

instructions.throttle-height: The throttle controls the height: more power climbs, less power sinks.
instructions.throttle-bursts: After each correction a short burst of throttle is needed. Holding high throttle makes the model climb out of the <hover>hover</hover>.
instructions.aileron-torque: The propeller torque tries to turn the model about its long axis. Aileron against the torque stops it. In the models these sources describe, that is right aileron.
instructions.rudder-elevator: Rudder and elevator keep the model vertical: rudder for left and right, elevator for forward and back.
instructions.small-early: Corrections should be small, short and early, not held.
instructions.belly-in-rudder: With the belly toward you, push the rudder stick toward the wing that is dropping.
instructions.exit-elevator: To leave the hover, push the elevator gently forward so the nose falls through the harrier attitude, then accelerate away.

notes.elevator-direction: Which way to move the elevator when the nose tilts toward or away from you: the sources do not say.
notes.throttle-style: Throttle changes: two sources use short bursts after each correction, one says to make small, smooth changes because a big change adds torque and rolls the model.

illustration.orientation: The animation shows the model entering by flying away and pulling up, with the <canopy>canopy</canopy> toward you. The sources do not confirm this. It is an illustration, as are stick travel and timing.

torque-roll.name: Torque roll
torque-roll.idea: A hover in which the model also turns about its long axis, driven by the propeller torque.

instructions.calm-air: Practise in calm air. Wind makes it much harder.

instructions.pull-vertical: Pull the model to a fully vertical <hover>hover</hover>. The <propeller>propeller</propeller> carries it.
instructions.let-it-turn: Do not counter the <torque>torque</torque>: in a clean hover the model starts to rotate by itself.

instructions.torque-turns: The <propeller>propeller</propeller> <torque>torque</torque> makes the model rotate about its long axis.
instructions.turns-left: The torque turns the model to the left.
instructions.rudder-elevator: Rudder and elevator keep the long axis of the model vertical.
instructions.throttle-steps: Adjust the throttle in small steps so the model neither climbs nor sinks.
instructions.large-throws: Large control surfaces and large <throws>throws</throws> help.
instructions.corrections-reverse: As the model turns, the elevator and rudder corrections change direction: correct by which way the nose leans, not by the stick labels.

instructions.aileron-stops: Aileron against the torque (right aileron) slows or stops the rotation.

notes.exit: How to end the <torqueRoll>torque roll</torqueRoll> and leave the <hover>hover</hover>: the sources give no confirmed instruction.

illustration.orientation: The animation shows a <hover>hover</hover> with the <canopy>canopy</canopy> toward you. The sources do not say which side faces you. It is an illustration, as are stick travel and timing.
illustration.viewpoint: The sources say the <torque>torque</torque> turns the model to the left, but not from which viewpoint. The animation shows it rolling to the left as seen from behind the model.

rolling-harrier.name: Rolling harrier
rolling-harrier.idea: A harrier in which the model also rolls continuously about its long axis while holding its height.

instructions.slow-rolls: Practise slow rolls with <rudder>rudder</rudder> and <elevator>elevator</elevator> support before you try this.
instructions.high-rates: Set large control travel on rudder and elevator and reduced <expo>exponential</expo>, so inputs respond without delay.
instructions.advanced: This is an advanced figure that needs a lot of practice.

entry.title: Nose up and start the roll

instructions.from-harrier: Start from an established nose-high <harrier>harrier</harrier>, then command full <aileron>aileron</aileron> and begin to roll.
instructions.attitude: The sources give a nose-up <attitude>attitude</attitude> of roughly 35° to 60°.

instructions.aileron-full: Hold full aileron in one direction for the whole roll and release it only at the exit.
instructions.alternate: Rudder and elevator come in one after the other during each roll while the aileron stays fixed. The timing is the hard part.
instructions.rudder-knife: The rudder works hardest when the model is on its side. Near <upright>upright</upright> and near <inverted>inverted</inverted>, the elevator does the work.
instructions.elevator-sequence: Toward inverted, give down elevator. Coming back round to upright, change to up elevator.
instructions.throttle-hold: Use the throttle to hold height and keep the nose up: more power raises the nose, less lets it drop.
instructions.timing-drift: The timing of the rudder and elevator inputs decides which way the model drifts sideways.
instructions.slow-roll: If the roll gets slower, that is a sign of too little power: add throttle.

notes.throttle-start: Throttle at the start of the roll: one source adds a few clicks, one uses medium-to-low throttle, one cuts the power. There is no agreed rule.
notes.rudder-needed: Is the rudder needed? Most sources use it. Some say rolling with elevator only works but looks poor, and one says it is not workable.
notes.rudder-direction: Which way the rudder goes relative to the roll direction: only one source says it (against the roll at the first <knifeEdge>knife edge</knifeEdge>, so right rudder for a left roll, then left rudder at the second). No second source confirms it, and none gives the amount.

instructions.exit-inputs: Add power, release the aileron and reduce the elevator to return to normal forward flight.

illustration.direction: The animation rolls the model to the left, with the <rudder>rudder</rudder> toward the top of the model. Only one source gives a roll direction and a rudder direction (a left roll with right rudder at the first <knifeEdge>knife edge</knifeEdge>). Roll speed, stick travel and <throttle>throttle</throttle> are illustrations too.

flat-spin.name: Flat spin
flat-spin.idea: The model spins flat about the vertical axis, with power, while staying roughly level.

instructions.height: Start high. The exit needs more height than a conventional <spin>spin</spin>, because <airspeed>airspeed</airspeed> has to be rebuilt from a flat <attitude>attitude</attitude>.
instructions.models-differ: Not every model <flatSpin>flat spins</flatSpin>, and models differ widely in how well they enter and recover.
instructions.cg: A rearward centre of gravity helps the model to flat spin.
instructions.throws: Use large control <throws>throws</throws> on all controls.
instructions.simulator: Practise on a flight <simulator>simulator</simulator> first. The real model may behave differently.

instructions.from-spin: Start from an ordinary <spin>spin</spin>: slow the model, <stall>stall</stall> it, begin the spin, and only then flatten it.
instructions.bleed-speed: Bleed off the speed: reduce the <throttle>throttle</throttle> toward idle and raise the nose until the model stalls.
instructions.full-inputs: At entry the elevator is full up and the rudder is full toward the spin direction.

notes.aileron-entry: <aileron>Aileron</aileron> at entry: some sources say the same direction as the rudder, one says the opposite direction, one says it depends on the model.

instructions.hold-inputs: Once the <spin>spin</spin> is established, hold <elevator>elevator</elevator> and <rudder>rudder</rudder> at their large deflections while you tune the rest.
instructions.aileron-ease: To flatten the spin, bring the aileron slowly toward neutral or toward the opposite side, never abruptly.
instructions.add-throttle: Add some throttle to help flatten the spin and to keep the model from falling fast.
instructions.tail-authority: A little throttle gives the rudder and elevator more authority at the tail.

instructions.throttle-height: With <throttle>throttle</throttle> the model can hold its height or even climb. Without throttle it falls slowly.

notes.spin-rate: How to control the <spin>spin</spin> rate and how long to hold the spin: the sources give no confirmed instruction.

instructions.release: Centre or release the sticks. Some models then stop rotating on their own.
instructions.opposite-rudder: If it keeps rotating, give rudder opposite to the rotation.
instructions.more-turns: Releasing the sticks does not always stop it at once. Several more turns are possible.

notes.exit-throttle: <throttle>Throttle</throttle> during the exit: one source says idle until <airspeed>airspeed</airspeed> builds, but also that adding power speeds the recovery; two forum posters say power is what makes the exit possible.
notes.recoverable: Can a <flatSpin>flat spin</flatSpin> be exited at all? One wiki says a flat spin means losing the model. Other sources say the exit is routine with a suitable model and correct inputs.

illustration.illustration: The animation shows no <aileron>aileron</aileron>, because the sources disagree on its direction and amount. The <spin>spin</spin> direction (to the left), the <throttle>throttle</throttle> level and the stick travel are illustrations.

loop.name: Loop
loop.idea: The model flies a full circle in the vertical plane and levels out where it started.

instructions.full-power: Fly in straight and level with full throttle.

notes.power: Power: one source says any plane with an <elevator>elevator</elevator> and enough power can <loop>loop</loop>. Nothing is confirmed for <motorglider>motor gliders</motorglider>.
notes.min-height: Minimum height: the sources give no confirmed value.

instructions.up-elevator: Pull the elevator smoothly and firmly to start the climb.
instructions.vertical-plane: Keep the loop in one plane: small rudder and aileron corrections as needed.

instructions.throttle-back: On the way over and down, reduce the throttle so the model does not get too fast.

instructions.level-out: Come out of the <loop>loop</loop> level, at the height where you started.

split-s.name: Split S
split-s.idea: From upright level flight the model rolls onto its back, then pulls through a half loop downwards. It ends level, flying the other way, lower than it started.

illustration.direction: The sources do not say which way to roll. The animation rolls to the right.

instructions.start-high: Start high enough to finish the half <loop>loop</loop>.

notes.min-height: How high is high enough: the sources give no confirmed value.

instructions.half-roll: Roll the model half a turn onto its back with the aileron.

instructions.pull-at-once: Pull the elevator straight after the roll, without flying inverted for long.
instructions.altitude-for-speed: The model trades height for speed: it gets faster on the way down.

instructions.level-reverse: The model ends <upright>upright</upright> and level, flying the opposite way, lower than it started.

roll.name: Roll
roll.idea: The model turns once around its long axis and stays on a straight line.

illustration.direction: The sources do not say which way to roll. The animation rolls to the left.
illustration.rudder: The animation shows no <rudder>rudder</rudder>, because only one source describes it.

instructions.level-entry: Start from straight and level flight at a steady speed.

instructions.aileron-rolls: The aileron makes the roll. Hold it in the same direction until the roll is done.
instructions.up-elevator: Add some up elevator in the first part of the roll.

notes.elevator-order: Order at the start: one source adds the up elevator first and then the aileron, another starts with the aileron and adds the up elevator past 45 degrees of <bank>bank</bank>.
notes.rudder: <rudder>Rudder</rudder>: only one source describes it in detail.

instructions.down-elevator-inverted: When the model is inverted, release the up elevator and add a little down elevator so it does not lose height.

instructions.stop-upright: Stop the roll when the model is upright again: bring the aileron back to centre.

instructions.level-flight: The model keeps its height and its heading through the roll.

stall-turn.name: Stall turn
stall-turn.idea: The model climbs straight up, pivots on the spot at the top, dives back down the same line and flies out the opposite way. Also called hammerhead.

illustration.direction: The sources do not say to which side the model swings round. The animation swings it away from the pilot, with full left <rudder>rudder</rudder>.
illustration.aileron: The animation shows no <aileron>aileron</aileron>, because only one source describes it.

notes.min-height: Minimum height: the sources give no confirmed value.

instructions.vertical-climb: Pull a quarter <loop>loop</loop> into a vertical climb and keep the climb straight.
instructions.throttle-not-closed: Reduce the throttle towards the top, but do not close it completely: the rudder needs airflow.

notes.propwash: <motorglider>Motor gliders</motorglider>: the sources rely on the <propeller>propeller</propeller> blowing air over the rudder. None says what to do with a stopped or folded propeller; one source says the rudder must then be used earlier, while the model still has forward speed.

instructions.full-rudder: At the top, as the climb runs out, apply full rudder.
instructions.tight-pivot: The model pivots almost on the spot.

instructions.dive-and-pull-out: Let the model dive straight down, then pull out with the elevator.

notes.throttle-dive: <throttle>Throttle</throttle> in the dive: one source adds power when pulling out, another keeps the throttle closed until the dive has built up speed.

instructions.opposite-direction: The model flies out level, in the opposite direction.

inverted-flight.name: Inverted flight
inverted-flight.idea: The model rolls onto its back, flies a straight line upside down and rolls back upright.

illustration.direction: The sources do not say which way to roll. The animation rolls to the right and back the same way. How long the model stays <inverted>inverted</inverted>, and the stick travel, are illustrations too.

instructions.level-add-power: Start from straight and level flight and add some throttle if needed.

instructions.half-roll: Roll half a turn onto the back with the aileron.
instructions.centre-aileron: When the wings are level, inverted, bring the aileron back to centre.

instructions.hold-elevator: Push the elevator forward a little to hold the height.
instructions.reversed: Elevator and rudder work the other way round from your view; the aileron does not.
instructions.push-amount: Too much forward elevator <stall>stalls</stall> or dives the model, too little loses height.
instructions.stall-speed: The stall speed is higher <inverted>inverted</inverted>: do not fly too slowly.
instructions.dihedral: Models with dihedral or V-form want to roll back <upright>upright</upright>, so fly actively.

notes.duration: How long to hold: one source says only 2 to 3 seconds at first; no second source.
notes.motor-glider: <motorglider>Motor gliders</motorglider>: no source covers them. One source says gliders and cambered trainers need a lot of forward elevator and speed inverted.
notes.amount: How much forward elevator: the sources give no value.

instructions.roll-out: Roll the model back upright with the aileron. Do not pull out of it.
instructions.enough-height: Practise with enough height to recover.

settings.title: Settings
settings.modeHint: Mode 2: throttle on the left stick. Mode 1: throttle on the right stick.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.metaDescription: Answers to common questions about StickScope: where the instructions come from, what the yellow-orange glow means, Mode 1 and Mode 2, and privacy.

what.a: StickScope is a free trainer for RC pilots. For each manoeuvre a 3D model and both transmitter sticks move together in slow motion, so you can see which stick movement leads to which flight. It runs in your browser, there is nothing to install.

sources.q: Where do the instructions come from?
sources.a: Every instruction is confirmed by at least two independent sources, for example different authors or publishers. The sources are listed with each figure. Where sources disagree or say nothing, the page shows a note instead of guessing.

real.q: Is the animation measured flight data?
real.a: No. The flight path, the stick travel and the timing are an illustration that makes the movement easy to follow. Parts of the animation that the sources do not confirm are marked as Illustration on the figure page.

glow.q: What does the yellow-orange glow mean?
glow.a: A control surface that is deflected glows yellow-orange, on the model, in the control schematic and in the flight-path overview. The stronger the glow, the more deflection. The glow fades for about a second.

mode.q: How do I switch between Mode 1 and Mode 2?
mode.a: Open the settings with the gear icon at the top right, or tap the mode label above the sticks. The switch only changes which stick shows which function. The figure itself stays the same.

simulator.q: Can I learn a manoeuvre with StickScope?
simulator.a: StickScope shows what the sticks do. Watch the figure first, then fly it in your simulator.

phone.q: Does it work on a phone?
phone.a: Yes, in the browser of your phone or tablet. Drag in the 3D view to look at the model from any side.

sound.a: An optional sound that follows the throttle. It is off on every visit and is generated in your browser.

privacy.a: There is no account, no cookies, no visitor counting and no analytics. Your choices (colour scheme, stick mode, last category, open windows) are stored only in your browser. Details are in the privacy policy.

more.q: Which manoeuvres are there, and will there be more?
more.a: The figures are sorted into beginner, advanced, pro and motor glider, and chosen in the manoeuvre browser. The set grows step by step.

mistake.q: I found a mistake or have a suggestion.
mistake.a: Please write to the e-mail address in the legal notice. Correctness is the main goal, so a hint with a source is especially welcome.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: Short explanations of the words you meet in RC and 3D flying. Tap an underlined word in an instruction to see its explanation.
glossary.note: These explanations describe what the words mean. They are not flying instructions.

transmitter.name: Transmitter
transmitter.text: The handheld radio with the control sticks. It sends your stick movements to the receiver in the model.

stick.name: Stick
stick.text: One of the two control levers on the transmitter. Each stick moves in two directions, so the two sticks give four controls: throttle, rudder, elevator and aileron.

mode.name: Stick mode (Mode 1 / Mode 2)
mode.text: Which function sits on which stick. In Mode 2, the most common layout, the left stick has throttle and rudder and the right stick has elevator and aileron. In Mode 1, throttle and elevator swap places. You can switch the mode in the StickScope settings.

throttle.name: Throttle
throttle.text: Controls the motor power, from idle to full power. It is the only one of the four controls that does not move a control surface. In a hover or harrier the throttle holds the height.

aileron.name: Aileron
aileron.text: The control surfaces on the rear edge of the wings. They move in opposite directions and roll the model about its long axis.

elevator.name: Elevator
elevator.text: The control surface on the horizontal tail. It tilts the nose up or down (pitch). Pulling the stick toward you raises the nose.

rudder.name: Rudder
rudder.text: The control surface on the vertical tail. It swings the nose to the left or right (yaw). In 3D flying it also holds the model in a knife edge and turns it around at the top of a stall turn.

expo.name: Expo (exponential)
expo.text: A transmitter setting that makes a control less sensitive around the stick centre, while full stick still gives full deflection. Small corrections become gentler, large inputs stay strong.

dualRates.name: Dual rates
dualRates.text: A transmitter setting with two (or more) levels for the maximum control deflection, switched in flight. The high level is the one for 3D flying; the low level calms the model down, for example for take-off and landing.

throws.name: Control throw
throws.text: How far a control surface moves from its neutral position. 3D models use large control surfaces and large throws, so they still respond when they fly very slowly.

trim.name: Trim
trim.text: A small shift of the neutral position of a control, set so that the model flies straight and level with the sticks centred and hands off.

mixing.name: Mixing
mixing.text: Combining two controls so that one stick movement drives more than one servo, for example aileron together with rudder. Mixers are set up in the transmitter.

servo.name: Servo
servo.text: The small motor unit that moves a control surface. It follows the signal from the receiver.

receiver.name: Receiver
receiver.text: The unit in the model that picks up the radio signal and passes it on to the servos and the speed controller.

failsafe.name: Failsafe
failsafe.text: A setting that decides what the model does when the radio link is lost, for example throttle to idle. It is set up before the first flight.

esc.name: Speed controller (ESC)
esc.text: The electronic unit that controls the speed of an electric motor from the throttle signal. ESC stands for electronic speed controller.

simulator.name: Flight simulator
simulator.text: Software on a computer or phone for practising with a virtual model, usually with a real transmitter plugged in. StickScope shows the manoeuvres; the simulator is where you try them.

fuselage.name: Fuselage
fuselage.text: The main body of the model, to which wings and tail are attached.

wing.name: Wing
wing.text: The surfaces that carry the model. The ailerons sit on their rear edge.

tail.name: Tail (empennage)
tail.text: The rear group of surfaces: the horizontal stabilizer with the elevator and the vertical fin with the rudder.

horizontalStabilizer.name: Horizontal stabilizer
horizontalStabilizer.text: The fixed part of the tail that keeps the model stable in pitch. The elevator is hinged to its rear edge.

fin.name: Fin (vertical stabilizer)
fin.text: The fixed vertical part of the tail that keeps the model stable in yaw. The rudder is hinged to its rear edge.

canopy.name: Canopy
canopy.text: The cover over the cockpit of the model, usually in a different colour. In StickScope the canopy tells you the top side: you see it when you look at the model from above.

landingGear.name: Landing gear
landingGear.text: The wheels and struts the model takes off and lands on. They also serve as a direction cue: toward the landing gear means toward the underside (belly) of the model.

propeller.name: Propeller
propeller.text: The rotating blades that produce the thrust. In a hover the model hangs on its propeller.

spinner.name: Spinner
spinner.text: The cone that covers the hub of the propeller.

cg.name: Centre of gravity (CG)
cg.text: The point where the model balances. Where it sits has a strong effect on how stable or lively the model flies. The manufacturer states a value for each model, and you set it by shifting weight such as the battery.

wingLoading.name: Wing loading
wingLoading.text: The weight of the model divided by its wing area. The lower it is, the slower the model can fly.

thrustToWeight.name: Thrust-to-weight ratio
thrustToWeight.text: How the thrust of the propeller compares to the weight of the model. At a ratio of about one or more, the model can hang on its propeller in a hover.

wingspan.name: Wingspan
wingspan.text: The distance from one wing tip to the other. It is the usual measure of the size of a model.

airfoil.name: Airfoil
airfoil.text: The cross-section shape of a wing.

leadingEdge.name: Leading edge
leadingEdge.text: The front edge of a wing, tailplane or fin.

trailingEdge.name: Trailing edge
trailingEdge.text: The rear edge of a wing, tailplane or fin, where the control surfaces sit.

motorglider.name: Motor glider
motorglider.text: A glider with a motor, often with a folding propeller. Its weight, power and flight behaviour differ from a pure 3D model, so the instructions do not fit every motor glider.

propwash.name: Propwash
propwash.text: The air stream that the propeller blows back over the model. Control surfaces in this stream still work when the model itself is almost standing still.

rollAxis.name: Roll (axis)
rollAxis.text: Rotation about the long axis of the model, from nose to tail. The ailerons roll the model. Positive roll in StickScope means right wing down.

pitch.name: Pitch
pitch.text: Rotation of the nose up or down, about the axis along the wings. The elevator pitches the model.

yaw.name: Yaw
yaw.text: Rotation of the nose to the left or right, about the vertical axis. The rudder yaws the model.

attitude.name: Attitude
attitude.text: How the model is oriented in space: nose up or down, rolled, upright or inverted, regardless of where it is moving. Attitude and flight path are different things: a hovering model has a vertical attitude but hardly moves.

bank.name: Bank
bank.text: A roll angle: the model leans to one side, with the wings not level.

angleOfAttack.name: Angle of attack
angleOfAttack.text: The angle between the wing and the oncoming air. Above a critical angle the air flow separates from the wing and the wing stalls.

stall.name: Stall
stall.text: Loss of lift when the angle of attack gets too big (often at low speed). A stalled wing no longer carries the model, which sinks. Many 3D figures fly in or near the stall on purpose.

postStall.name: Post-stall (high alpha)
postStall.text: Flying beyond the stall angle, at a very high angle of attack and very low speed. The model is held up by the propeller and steered by large control surfaces. The harrier is an example.

spin.name: Spin
spin.text: A stalled, rotating fall in which the model turns about a vertical axis while one wing is stalled more than the other. Recovery needs a specific control input.

airspeed.name: Airspeed
airspeed.text: The speed of the model through the air, not over the ground. Control surfaces need airflow, so they get weak at low airspeed unless the propeller blows air over them.

lift.name: Lift
lift.text: The upward force that the wings produce from the air flowing past them.

drag.name: Drag
drag.text: The air resistance that slows the model down.

thrust.name: Thrust
thrust.text: The pull the propeller produces. More throttle gives more thrust.

torque.name: Propeller torque
torque.text: The motor turns the propeller one way and the reaction turns the model the other way about its long axis. The torque roll uses this effect. The direction depends on the model; the propeller direction is not fixed.

adverseYaw.name: Adverse yaw
adverseYaw.text: When rolling with the ailerons the nose briefly swings the opposite way, because the wing that goes down has more drag. The rudder, a mixer or aileron differential can counter it.

straightLevel.name: Straight and level
straightLevel.text: Flying in a straight line at constant height with the wings level.

upright.name: Upright flight
upright.text: Normal flight, with the canopy facing up.

inverted.name: Inverted flight
inverted.text: Flight on the back, with the canopy facing down. To hold the nose up the elevator stick has to be pushed instead of pulled.

pullPush.name: Pull / push
pullPush.text: Moving the elevator stick toward you (pull) or away from you (push). In upright flight pulling raises the nose and pushing lowers it.

line.name: Upline / downline
line.text: A straight stretch of the flight path that climbs (upline) or descends (downline), in many figures a vertical one.

pullOut.name: Pull-out
pullOut.text: Ending a dive by pulling the elevator so the model returns to level flight.

aerobatics.name: Aerobatics
aerobatics.text: Flying figures that do not occur in normal flight, such as loops and rolls.

threeD.name: 3D flying
threeD.text: A style of aerobatics in which the model flies very slowly, near or beyond the stall or hanging on its propeller, with oversized control surfaces and plenty of power. Hover, harrier and torque roll are 3D figures.

loop.name: Loop
loop.text: The model flies a full circle in the vertical plane and levels out where it started.

rollFigure.name: Roll (figure)
rollFigure.text: The model turns once around its long axis and stays on a straight line.

barrelRoll.name: Barrel roll
barrelRoll.text: A roll flown on a corkscrew path around an imaginary straight line, instead of on the line itself.

snapRoll.name: Snap roll
snapRoll.text: A very fast roll that starts with a sharp pull on the elevator together with rudder and aileron in the roll direction. The wing is stalled while the model turns.

splitS.name: Split S
splitS.text: From upright level flight the model rolls onto its back, then pulls through a half loop downwards. It ends level, flying the other way, lower than it started.

immelmann.name: Immelmann
immelmann.text: A half loop upwards followed by a half roll at the top. The model ends upright, flying the other way, higher than it started. It is the counterpart of the split S.

cubanEight.name: Cuban eight
cubanEight.text: A figure eight made of two loop sections, each followed by a half roll on a diagonal line.

rollingCircle.name: Rolling circle
rollingCircle.text: A loop flown while the model rolls continuously about its long axis.

stallTurn.name: Stall turn (hammerhead)
stallTurn.text: The model climbs straight up, pivots on the spot at the top, dives back down the same line and flies out the opposite way. Also called hammerhead.

knifeEdge.name: Knife edge
knifeEdge.text: The model flies straight on its side. The rudder holds it there.

hover.name: Hover
hover.text: The model hangs vertically on its propeller, almost standing in place. The throttle holds the height. Also called prop hang.

harrier.name: Harrier
harrier.text: Slow flight with the nose about 45° up, in post-stall. The elevator sets the nose attitude, the throttle holds the height.

rollingHarrier.name: Rolling harrier
rollingHarrier.text: A harrier in which the model also rolls continuously about its long axis while holding its height.

torqueRoll.name: Torque roll
torqueRoll.text: A hover in which the model also turns about its long axis, driven by the propeller torque.

flatSpin.name: Flat spin
flatSpin.text: The model spins flat about the vertical axis, with power, while staying roughly level.

elevatorFigure.name: Elevator (figure)
elevatorFigure.text: The model sinks on a steep to nearly vertical line with the elevator pulled fully, nose high and stalled.

tumble.name: Tumble
tumble.text: The model somersaults end over end, about the axis along its wings, in a very small radius and with hardly any forward speed.

tailslide.name: Tailslide
tailslide.text: The model slides backwards, tail first, in a vertical attitude.

waterfall.name: Waterfall
waterfall.text: The model climbs vertically until it slides backwards tail first, then flips over into a dive.

wall.name: Wall (pop-up)
wall.text: The model goes from level flight into a vertical attitude almost instantly, shedding its speed.

lomcovak.name: Lomcovák (Lomcevak)
lomcovak.text: A name for tumbling figures in which the tail swings over the nose. Sources describe several variants, so the exact figure differs from pilot to pilot.
